_comment: recipes.json — Canonical source of truth for all crafting recipes. All base_craft_time values are in seconds and should be tuned here, never hardcoded in game logic.

config._comment: Multiply all base_craft_time values by this for global tuning. Persistent upgrade 'craft_speed' reduces this multiplier.
config._comment_ev: Base eV cost per atomic mass unit for Atomic Assembler recipes. Recipe power_cost_ev = atomic_mass × atomic_assembler_ev_per_mass_unit. Tune this single value to rebalance the entire power economy.
config._comment_isotope_ev: Base eV cost per neutron added/removed in the Isotopic Manipulator.
config._comment_manual: Base manual craft time in seconds for tier 1 nucleons. More complex recipes scale from this.

raw_resources.name: Up Quark
raw_resources.codex: One of two quark types that make up protons and neutrons. Carries a +2/3 electric charge.

raw_resources.name: Down Quark
raw_resources.codex: One of two quark types that make up protons and neutrons. Carries a -1/3 electric charge.

raw_resources.name: Electron
raw_resources.codex: A fundamental particle with a negative charge. Orbits the nucleus of atoms and determines chemical bonding behavior.

recipes.name: Proton
recipes.codex: A positively charged nucleon made of 2 up quarks and 1 down quark, bound by the strong nuclear force. The number of protons in a nucleus defines which element it is.

recipes.name: Neutron
recipes.codex: A neutral nucleon made of 1 up quark and 2 down quarks. Neutrons stabilize the nucleus — changing the neutron count produces isotopes of the same element.

recipes._section: TIER 2 — ATOMIC (standard isotopes via Atomic Assembler)

recipes.name: Hydrogen
recipes.codex: The simplest and most abundant element in the universe. One proton, one electron — no neutrons in its most common form. The primary fuel of stars.

recipes.name: Helium

alternate_recipe.note: Fusion path produces alpha particles as byproduct energy source

recipes.codex: The second lightest element, produced in stellar cores through hydrogen fusion. Noble gas — chemically inert. Its nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is also known as an alpha particle.

recipes.name: Lithium
recipes.codex: A soft alkali metal and the lightest solid element. Critical in battery technology — the backbone of rechargeable batteries used in mobile devices.

recipes.name: Carbon
recipes.codex: The basis of all organic chemistry. Carbon's ability to form four bonds makes it the backbone of life. Also exists as graphite, diamond, and graphene.

recipes.name: Oxygen
recipes.codex: The third most abundant element in the universe. Highly reactive, essential for combustion and respiration. Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere.

recipes.name: Silicon
recipes.codex: A semiconductor at the heart of modern electronics. Silicon wafers are the foundation of processors, solar cells, and transistors.

recipes.name: Iron
recipes.codex: The most common element on Earth by mass. The endpoint of stellar fusion — stars cannot fuse elements heavier than iron without consuming more energy than they produce.

recipes.name: Uranium
recipes.codex: The heaviest naturally occurring element. Radioactive — decays slowly over billions of years. The primary fuel for nuclear fission reactors.

recipes.name: Deuterium
recipes.codex: A stable isotope of hydrogen with one neutron added. Found naturally in heavy water. Essential fuel for nuclear fusion reactions.

recipes.name: Tritium
recipes.codex: A radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons. Undergoes beta decay. Combined with deuterium in the most efficient known fusion reaction.

recipes.name: Carbon-14
recipes.codex: A radioactive isotope of carbon used in archaeological dating. Its predictable decay rate allows scientists to estimate the age of organic materials up to 50,000 years old.

recipes.name: Uranium-235
recipes.codex: The fissile isotope of uranium used in nuclear reactors and weapons. Splitting U-235 releases enormous energy and produces alpha particles as decay byproducts.

recipes.name: Alpha Particle
recipes.codex: Emitted during alpha decay of heavy radioactive isotopes. Equivalent to a helium-4 nucleus. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and used as a secondary energy currency.

recipes.name: Beta Particle
recipes.codex: Emitted during beta decay of unstable isotopes like Tritium and Carbon-14. A high-energy electron. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and fed back into the power grid.

buildings.name: Harvester
buildings._comment: Output rate is items/second. Works on any field type, outputs that field's resource.

special_upgrade.name: Nucleon Harvester
special_upgrade.description: Merges a positive-field and negative-field harvester into a single Nucleon Harvester. Player selects output: Proton or Neutron. Abstracts quark combination entirely.

buildings.codex: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Place on a field to begin harvesting. Positive fields yield Up Quarks, negative fields yield Down Quarks, lepton fields yield Electrons.

buildings.name: Strong Force Combiner
buildings.tutorial_note: First powered building. Placement triggers power system tutorial.
buildings.codex: Uses the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into nucleons. Requires a power source within range to operate.

buildings.name: Basic Generator
buildings.tutorial_note: Introduced immediately after Strong Force Combiner placement. Teaches power radius and energy grid.
buildings.codex: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.

buildings.name: Atomic Assembler
buildings._comment_ev: Power cost determined per recipe: atomic_mass × config.atomic_assembler_ev_per_mass_unit
buildings.codex: Combines protons, neutrons, and electrons into complete atoms. Power cost scales with the complexity of the element being assembled — heavier elements demand more energy.

buildings.name: Isotopic Manipulator
buildings._comment_rate: Slower than Atomic Assembler by default — isotope production is a specialised process
buildings.codex: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Radioactive isotopes produced here will emit decay particles over time if housed in a Radioactive Containment building.

buildings.name: Radioactive Containment
buildings._comment: Collects alpha/beta particles emitted by radioactive isotopes being produced inside. Feeds them to Resource Vault as secondary currency.
buildings.codex: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles as usable energy currency.
